To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Internal and privileged. Not for circulation to the Seller.

---

## Preliminary flags

1. **The "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" have no authority.** The Seller says [STANDARD] clauses were "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that we "have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." Nothing on our side confirms this, and under playbook §0.4 and §6.3 a counterparty's description of a position as agreed, cleared or standard does not bind us. I have reviewed every clause in full. We should tell the Seller in writing that we accept no pre-clearance.
2. **The Seller Update contradicts the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.** For example:
   - Bluefen is "addressed", but the letter (para 2) says there is no final consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied.
   - The incident is "not expected to be material", but the letter (para 6) says scope, access and notification are all undetermined.

   Where they conflict, the Disclosure Letter's factual admissions are the more reliable source.
3. **The cap and time limit match our fallbacks, but that does not authorise them.** The 20% cap and 18-month period are our conditional fallbacks. Neither has Amelia Frost's written authority, and neither may be offered or accepted on the strength of a matching number.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1), labelled [STANDARD].
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. The 20% fallback needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none has been given.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and the deductible structure strips the first AUD 250k of every recovery.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. Any limitation also applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims, with separate periods for fundamental, tax and fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at 24 months. The 18-month fallback is unapproved, and the "applies to all Claims" wording silently drags fundamental and fraud claims into the 18-month period.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap (AUD 24m) and at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright. Title and capacity are the core of what we are buying, and capping them at 20% for 18 months guts our protection.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert an express carve-out as non-negotiable. Under the playbook nobody may waive it, and the Seller's drafting would purport to limit fraud claims.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 5pm 22 Sept 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure against particular warranties only.
- **Recommendation:** Delete DL 1.1–1.2 and confine disclosure to specific matters fairly disclosed. Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure would neutralise the warranties.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Deletion of the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier should refer to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3. It imputes adviser and constructive knowledge to us and would bar claims for the very issues our diligence identified.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** "Addressed". Reasonable endeavours only, with the consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.
- **Facts (DL 2):** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of revenue (around 30%). There is no final consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** A Condition Precedent requiring an effective consent plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours are insufficient for a 30% customer, and the "addressed" label contradicts the Seller's own disclosure.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release "to be provided following Completion".
- **Facts (DL 3):** Not repaid, no discharge, and change-control and discharge provisions apply (cl 8.1 and 9.2).
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A post-Completion release would leave security over the target with no protection, and any fallback needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 in DD-005 bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. On-costs are unaddressed (DL 5).
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420k plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs either shown as a specific funds-flow line item (deducted as Debt or a transaction cost) or funded by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the silent exclusion. The bonuses are triggered by Completion, so without a line item and an indemnity the Company, and therefore we, would bear them.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate".
- **Facts (DL 4):** Transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. The AUD 180k open balance is not independently verified, and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering IP ownership and third-party claims arising from Ironquay materials, preserving the SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment). The AUD 180k should be treated as unverified either way.
- **Recommendation:** Broaden the indemnity. A payment-only indemnity does not cover the real risk, which is that ownership never passed. We should require payment evidence and an assignment as Completion deliverables.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
- **Facts (DL 6):** A download link went to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records are potentially affected. Access, scope and notification duty are all undetermined.
- **Buyer wants:** Covenants to preserve logs, complete the investigation and give regular updates before Completion, plus appropriate specific protection.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's materiality characterisation and require those covenants. The facts are unresolved, so we should assume neither a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure, nor their absence.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Facts (DL 8):** The disclosure is silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course, and DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of timing, scope and terminability before deciding treatment, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction either way.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label yet. Request the underlying terms and assess. The Seller's own disclosure does not support the characterisation.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** A single general regime applies to all Claims (cl 12.3, 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5), absorbing title, tax and IP.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations (Riverlark, bonuses, Debt) and covenants, with no hidden general override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "all Claims" wording and add express category-specific carve-outs and an order-of-precedence clause. As drafted, one sentence subordinates every specific protection to a 20% cap and 18-month period.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title to 100% of the shares is "evidenced by" the DD-012 share register.
- **Facts (DL 10):** The Seller itself concedes DD-012 is merely the source it relies on and that we have not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, such as an ASIC search, PPSR search, constitution, board and shareholder approvals, share certificates and confirmation of no options or rights.
- **Recommendation:** Reject reliance on DD-012 alone. An internal register supplied by the Seller is not independent proof, and the Riverlark security makes an encumbrance check essential.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Both treated as OPEN, with no assumption of resolution and no assumption of unlimited liability.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "settled" characterisation and keep tax and IP open for separate negotiation. No agreement exists on our side, and folding them into the general regime would lock in the Seller's cap and time limit.

---

## Recommended next steps

1. **Response to the Seller:** Reject the pre-categorisation and the claimed acceptance of the disclosure and limitation package, and confirm that all clauses remain open.
2. **Internal:** Do not offer the 20% cap or 18-month period unless and until Amelia Frost gives written authority identifying this draft.
3. **Diligence requests:**
   - Bluefen consent and evidence its conditions are satisfied
   - Riverlark payout letter and draft releases
   - Ironquay payment evidence and confirmatory assignment
   - DD-006 investigation logs and update
   - Sandbar contract terms
   - Independent title searches
   - Payroll and on-cost analysis for the DD-005 bonuses
4. **Mark-up:** Prepare a full SPA mark-up and Disclosure Letter mark-up on the positions above.
